title: Sickle cell variants, hemolytic and aplastic anemia, hemophilia, neutropenia
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's blood disorder (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for sickle cell-hemoglobin C disease.

HPI: Pt is a 32 y.o. male presenting for routine hematology follow-up. He has a known diagnosis of sickle cell-hemoglobin C disease. Pt reports feeling well today. No acute symptoms. Denies joint pain, chest pain, or any recent episodes of intense discomfort. He reports adherence to hydration and prophylactic regimen. Stable status throughout.

Medication List:
- Hydroxyurea 500mg BID
- Folic acid 1mg daily
- Fluconazole 200mg weekly

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fatigue, no weight changes.
Respiratory: No SOB, no cough.
MSK: No joint pain.
CV: No palpitations, no chest pain.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Works as a software engineer. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use. Lives with spouse and two children.

Family History: Father has hypertension. Mother has Type 2 DM. Sibling has Hb SC.

Recent Labs:
Hb: 9.2 g/dL
Hct: 28%
WBC: 8.5 x 10^9/L
Plt: 145 x 10^3/uL
Reticulocyte count: 2.1%

Vitals:
BP: 122/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Weight: 185 lbs

Exam:
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, oriented x3.
CV: RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmurs.
Resp: CTAB, no wheezes/crackles.
MSK: No erythema or swelling in joints.
Skin: No visible lesions.
Neuro: NAD.

Assessment:
1. Sickle cell-hemoglobin C disease: Stable. Pt is asymptomatic and tolerating current regimen well. No recent complications.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications.
2. Continue folic acid supplementation.
3. Routine labs to be drawn in 3 months.
4. Follow up in 3 months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed, 
L. Moreau, DO
05/14/2026
explanations: Sickle cell-hemoglobin C disease without crisis: D57.20 (HCC 108).

distractors.why: Hb SC is a separate sickle cell disorder (HCC 108), not Hb-SS.
It is a disease, not the trait.
